title: Health in depth
goal: Describe your symptoms precisely and say how long you've had them, mention allergies and conditions, book an appointment and follow a doctor's instructions.
intro:
In unit 9 you learned to say **منهنجو مٿو ڏکي ٿو**. Now you'll tell a doctor exactly what's wrong — **مون کي چڪر ٿا اچن**, **سور اچي وڃي ٿو**, **مون کي پينسلين کان الرجي آهي** — and, crucially, **for how long**: Sindhi says *I have had a fever for three days* with a simple present and **کان**: **مون کي ٽن ڏينهن کان بخار آهي**.

You'll also learn the instruction forms that doctors and pharmacists use — **ڏينهن ۾ ٻه ڀيرا، ماني کان پوءِ کائجو** — and the words you need for clinics, tests and hospital visits. Expect a lot of English in a Sindhi doctor's mouth: **ٽيسٽ**, **شوگر**, **بي پي**, **چيڪ اپ**.

grammar.title: How long: 'I've had it for three days' — time + کان + present
grammar.body:
English needs the present perfect for this: *I **have had** a fever for three days*, *I **have been living** here for two years*. Sindhi simply uses the **present**, and marks the starting point with **کان** 'from':

**مون کي ٽن ڏينهن کان بخار آهي** — 'to me, from three days, fever is'
**مان ٻن سالن کان ڪراچيءَ ۾ رهان ٿو** — I've been living in Karachi for two years
**هوءَ صبح کان سمهي پئي آهي** — she's been asleep since the morning

So **کان** covers both English *for* and *since*: ٻن ڏينهن کان 'for two days', سومر کان 'since Monday', ڪالهه کان 'since yesterday', صبح کان 'since this morning'.

A number + time word before کان goes into the **oblique**: ٻه ڏينهن → **ٻن ڏينهن** کان, ٽي سال → **ٽن سالن** کان, هڪ هفتو → **هڪ هفتي** کان, هڪ مهينو → **هڪ مهيني** کان.

**Asking:** **ڪڏهن کان؟** 'since when?' · **ڪيترن ڏينهن کان؟** 'for how many days?'
**'It's been …':** ٽي ڏينهن **ٿي ويا آهن** 'it's been three days'.

**The trap:** for a period that is **over**, don't use کان — just the time in the plain form and a past verb: مان **ٽي ڏينهن** اسپتال ۾ رهيس 'I was in hospital for three days' (and now I'm out). With کان and a present verb, it is **still going on**. And remember **اڳ** (unit 16) is 'ago': ٽي ڏينهن **اڳ** 'three days ago'.

grammar.title: Following instructions: کائجو، نه پيئجو، ماني کان پوءِ
grammar.body:
Doctors and pharmacists give instructions in the gentle **-jo** form you met in unit 18. It is polite, and it means 'from now on, (please) do …' — exactly right for a course of treatment:

**کائجو** 'take (lit. eat)' · **پيئجو** 'drink' · **لڳائجو** 'apply (cream)' · **ڪجو** 'do' · **اچجو** 'come' · **ڏجو** 'give'
Negative: **نه کائجو**، **نه پيئجو**، **نه ڇڏجو** 'don't stop'.

**Medicine is eaten.** Tablets and even syrups are **کائڻ** (or پيئڻ for liquids): دوا کائجو. You'll also hear دوا وٺڻ, but کائڻ is the everyday verb.

**When:** **ڏينهن ۾ ٻه ڀيرا** 'twice a day' · **صبح شام** 'morning and evening' · **ماني کان اڳ / پوءِ** 'before / after food' · **خالي پيٽ** 'on an empty stomach' · **سمهڻ کان اڳ** 'before bed' · **پنج ڏينهن تائين** 'for five days' (a course of treatment uses تائين).
**What to avoid:** X **کان پرهيز ڪجو** 'cut out X'.

On labels and leaflets you'll see the impersonal **-ij-** form from unit 31: **ماني کان اڳ کائجي** 'to be taken before food', **ٻارن کان پري رکجي** 'keep away from children'.

For advice, use گهرجي (unit 9): توهان کي آرام ڪرڻ گهرجي. For a firm instruction: توهان کي … ڪرڻو پوندو.

culture:
Most people in Sindh see a doctor at a private evening **ڪلينڪ**: you turn up, give your name and wait your turn (**نمبر**). Doctors are **ڊاڪٽر صاحب** / **ڊاڪٽر صاحبه**, and they switch freely into English for medical words — **بي پي**, **شوگر**, **انفيڪشن**, **رپورٽ** — so don't be afraid to use the English term. Big public hospitals include the Civil Hospitals in Karachi and Hyderabad, LUMHS at Jamshoro and Chandka in Larkana; private ones like the Aga Khan University Hospital in Karachi are expensive.

Pharmacies (**ميڊيڪل اسٽور**) will often sell medicine without a prescription and give advice on the spot, and many patients expect a **ڊرپ** (drip) or an injection for a quick recovery. Home wisdom matters too: foods are 'hot' or 'cold' in nature, so with a cough you'll be told to avoid cold water, rice and yoghurt.

Visiting someone who is ill (**بيمار پرسي**) is a social duty: you go to the house or the hospital, take fruit or juice, sit a while and say **الله شفا ڏئي** 'may God heal you'. Ask **هاڻي طبيعت ڪيئن آهي؟** and **ڪو فرق پيو؟** — and expect to be offered tea even in the hospital corridor.

tip.title: Saying exactly what's wrong
tip.body:
- Most symptoms use **کي + آهي**: مون کي **خارش** آهي.
- Some 'come' to you: مون کي **چڪر ٿا اچن** (pl), **الٽي پئي اچي**.
- A place in the body + **۾**: پير **۾** سوڄ آهي.
- 'Comes and goes' = **اچي وڃي ٿو**.

lessons.title: Since when? How long?

tip.title: ٽن ڏينهن کان — for three days
tip.body:
- Sindhi uses the **present** + time + **کان**: مون کي ٽن ڏينهن **کان** بخار **آهي** 'I've had a fever for three days'.
- کان = both 'for' and 'since': ڪالهه کان، سومر کان.
- Number + time goes oblique: **ٻن ڏينهن** کان، **هڪ هفتي** کان.
- Finished period: no کان — مان ٽي ڏينهن اسپتال ۾ رهيس.

sentences.en: Get a blood test, then bring the report.

sentences.native: ايڪسري ۾ ڪجهه به نه آيو.
sentences.roman: eksre meṃ kujhu bi na āyo.
sentences.en: Nothing showed up on the X-ray.

sentences.native: ٽيسٽ جي رپورٽ ڪڏهن ملندي؟
sentences.roman: ṭesṭa jī riporṭa kaɗahiṃ milandī?
sentences.en: When will the test report be ready?

sentences.native: شوگر ۾ مٺو نه کائڻ گهرجي.
sentences.roman: shūgara meṃ miṭho na khāiṇu ghurje.
sentences.en: If you're diabetic you shouldn't eat sweet things.

sentences.native: ٽيسٽ لاءِ ٿورو رت ڏيڻو پوندو.
sentences.roman: ṭesṭa lāi thoro ratu ɗiyaṇo pavando.
sentences.en: You'll have to give a little blood for the test.

lessons.title: Following the doctor's orders

tip.title: Doctor's instructions: کائجو، نه پيئجو
tip.body:
- Instructions use the gentle **-jo** form: **کائجو** 'take', **پيئجو** 'drink', **ڪجو** 'do', **اچجو** 'come back'.
- Negative: **نه** before it: ٿڌو پاڻي **نه پيئجو**.
- Medicine is 'eaten': دوا **کائجو**.
- When: ڏينهن ۾ ٻه ڀيرا · ماني کان پوءِ · خالي پيٽ · سمهڻ کان اڳ.

new: ڏينهن ۾ ٻه ڀيرا، ماني کان پوءِ.

sentences.native: هي دوا ڏينهن ۾ ٻه ڀيرا، ماني کان پوءِ کائجو.
sentences.roman: hī davā ɗīṃha meṃ ɓa bherā, mānī khāṃ poi khāijo.
sentences.en: Take this medicine twice a day, after food.

sentences.native: هي گوري خالي پيٽ کائجو، صبح جو سوير.
sentences.roman: hī gorī xālī peṭa khāijo, subuh jo sver.
sentences.en: Take this tablet on an empty stomach, first thing in the morning.

sentences.native: ٿڌو پاڻي نه پيئجو، ۽ آرام ڪجو.
sentences.roman: thadho pāṇī na pījo, ai ārāmu kajo.
sentences.en: Don't drink cold water, and get some rest.

sentences.native: ٻار کي اڌ خوراڪ ڏجو.
sentences.roman: ɓāra khe adhu xurāka ɗijo.
sentences.en: Give the child half a dose.

sentences.native: کنڊ ۽ لوڻ کان پرهيز ڪجو.
sentences.roman: khanḍa ai lūṇa khāṃ parhezu kajo.
sentences.en: Cut out sugar and salt.

sentences.native: دوا پوري کائجو، اڌ ۾ نه ڇڏجو.
sentences.roman: davā pūrī khāijo, adha meṃ na chhaɗijo.
sentences.en: Finish the whole course; don't stop halfway.

sentences.native: سمهڻ کان اڳ هي شربت پيئجو.
sentences.roman: sumhaṇa khāṃ aɠu hī sharbatu pījo.
sentences.en: Drink this syrup before bed.

sentences.native: احتياط ڪجو! ٻاهر ڏاڍي گرمي آهي.
sentences.roman: ehtiyāta kajo! ɓāhari ɗāḍhī garmī āhe.
sentences.en: Take care! It's really hot outside.

sentences.native: ڊاڪٽر چيو ته ٽن ڏينهن کان پوءِ وري اچجو.
sentences.roman: ḍākṭara chayo ta ṭin ɗīṃhan khāṃ poi varī achijo.
sentences.en: The doctor said to come back after three days.

sentences.native: توهان کي گهڻو پاڻي پيئڻ گهرجي.
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ khe ghaṇo pāṇī pīaṇu ghurje.
sentences.en: You should drink plenty of water.

lessons.title: Clinics, appointments and hospital
new: ڊاڪٽر صاحب سان اپائنٽمينٽ ملي سگهي ٿي؟
هن کي اسپتال ۾ داخل ڪيو ويو آهي.

sentences.native: ڊاڪٽر صاحب سان اپائنٽمينٽ ملي سگهي ٿي؟ سڀاڻي شام جو؟
sentences.roman: ḍākṭar sāhib sāṃ apāinṭmenṭa milī saghe thī? subhāṇe shāma jo?
sentences.en: Can I get an appointment with the doctor? Tomorrow evening?

sentences.native: ڪلينڪ شام جو ڇهين وڳي کان ڏهين وڳي تائين آهي.
sentences.roman: kalīnika shāma jo chhahīṃ vaɠe khāṃ ɗahīṃ vaɠe tāīṃ āhe.
sentences.en: The clinic is open from six to ten in the evening.

sentences.native: سال ۾ هڪ ڀيرو چيڪ اپ ڪرائڻ گهرجي.
sentences.roman: sāla meṃ hiku bhero chek apu karāiṇu ghurje.
sentences.en: You should have a check-up once a year.

sentences.native: جلدي ڪريو، ايمرجنسيءَ ۾ هلو!
sentences.roman: jaldī karyo, emarjansīa meṃ halo!
sentences.en: Quick, let's get to A&E!

sentences.native: هن کي اسپتال ۾ داخل ڪيو ويو آهي. هاڻي ٺيڪ آهي.
sentences.roman: hun khe ispatāla meṃ dāxilu kayo vayo āhe. hāṇe ṭhīku āhe.
sentences.en: He's been admitted to hospital. He's OK now.

sentences.native: منهنجي ناني ٻن ڏينهن کان اسپتال ۾ داخل آهي.
sentences.roman: munhinjī nānī ɓin ɗīṃhan khāṃ ispatāla meṃ dāxilu āhe.
sentences.en: My grandmother has been in hospital for two days.

sentences.native: توهان کي ڇا تڪليف آهي؟ مٿي ۾ سور آهي؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ khe chhā takalīfa āhe? mathe meṃ sūru āhe?
sentences.en: What's the problem? Have you got a headache?

sentences.native: ڪلينڪ ۾ ڏاڍا ماڻهو هئا.
sentences.roman: kalīnika meṃ ɗāḍhā māṇhū huā.
sentences.en: The clinic was packed.

sentences.native: اسين هن کي ڏسڻ لاءِ اسپتال وياسين.
sentences.roman: asīṃ hun khe ɗisaṇa lāi ispatāla vayāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We went to the hospital to see him.
